run 0852ea7f30d2, naive mode, blinded 0.1.0, 2.1.302 (Claude Code). train 2026-10-01T00:00:00, validation 2026-10-01T12:05:00, test 2026-10-01T18:05:00 to 2026-10-02T00:00:00.

1. Verdict

On the locked test window (18:05:00-00:00:00), arb strategy cvm_bnc_fair_ret2s on ATUSDT_MEXC hedged on ATUSDT_BINANCE, under the risk-averse queue model, the worse of the two, made +6.5 bps a fill net of a 10 bps hedge fee over 49 fills, +0.29 USD at a 10.2 USD size (90% CI +0.08 to +0.52 USD), at a Sharpe per sqrt-hour of +0.94; 4% picked off, drifting 15 USD of coin to ATUSDT_BINANCE; the counterparty is one flow of 3,582 prints a day. It made no transfer between the venues on test.

Judged under rules v3.

Fee verdict: profitable at the brief's 10 bps taker fee; the 90% interval of net bps/hour on the score's blocks and draws is +820.6 to +5477.5, and it stays above zero at a taker fee of 11.72 bps or lower (break-even 16.63 bps).

The fills are the strategy as written: a strategy built for a rebate would quote differently.

3. Deflation

A naive run scores whatever window the agent asks for, so it has no validation blocks to deflate with. The protected run beside it does the deflation.

4. The signal

Shown on train, validation and test, by edge and then by archetype. Each archetype's pick is the rule of a families run kept to its own trials: the final strategy's, else the last released, else the best on validation. Test appears only when the final strategy was scored there.

Speed & information: paid for reaching a price first

Paid for reaching a price first. The other side is a stale quote or a slower reader, and the race only gets faster.

cross_venue_arbitrage: Cross-venue arbitrage

Pairs: ATUSDT_MEXC over ATUSDT_BINANCE, no cross_venue_arbitrage strategy was accepted; the declared pair

Fitted on the trailing 10m before each 10m clock window and held through it; bands at z 2 in and 0.5 out, from the brief's pairs defaults.

The spread is the log mid of A less the hedge ratio times that of B, here less its walk-forward mean, in bps. Its level jumps at every refit, so the mean is taken off. The dashed lines are where the strategy goes in, the dotted ones where it comes out, and the shading is where it held the spread.

The hedge ratio, the units of B the spread holds against one of A, fitted on the window before each clock window. A ratio that wanders makes the B leg trade at every refit.

How fast the spread came back inside each clock window: the half-life of an AR(1) fit. An open circle is a window where it did not come back at all. The dashed line is what the same fit reads on a pure random walk in a window this long, since the fitted slope sits below 1 even with no reversion: only points well under it show the spread coming back.

In the markout fan of the spread, every time its z-score went past the entry band of ±2 counts as a trade back toward the mean: short the spread when z is high, long when it is low. Events are at least 70 s apart. The line is the average move of the spread in that direction, at the hedge ratio of the moment, with two standard errors either side. A spread that reverts rises after zero. Breaking even takes crossing the spread of both legs twice, the B leg scaled by the hedge ratio, and the fees of both on top.

The strategy: cvm_bnc_fair_ret2s (trial 42), the final strategy

Quoted on ATUSDT_MEXC and every fill hedged on ATUSDT_BINANCE as a taker at its depth as-of the hedge's arrival. Four fill models, each its own closed loop, with a trade through the quote filling no more than its print. Per fill, in bps of the fill at the hedge venue's mid: captured, the maker leg against that mid; delay, its move until the hedge arrived; slippage, the hedge against the mid then; fees, both legs'; net, their sum. Picked off is a fill whose price that mid had already passed; drift is the USD of coin a day moved onto the quote venue. The judge scores the lower of RA's and PR's Sharpe on net per block, both legs, each on blocks at least as long as its holds (the brief's 5 min).

The half hour of the last segment with the most fills of the scored model: both venues' touches, the quotes resting on the quote venue, each fill and the hedge it sent.

How it dies. The deep venue moves through your quote before you can cancel (picked off); the hedge fee and half spread eat the distance; the thin venue's flow stops, or re-prices around you; the coin piles up on one venue and must be moved.

cvm_bnc_fair_ret2s
import polars as pl
import blinded as bl

x = bl.cross_venue_making(quote="ATUSDT_MEXC", hedge="ATUSDT_BINANCE")


@x.strategy(requires=["bnc_ret_2s_cvm"])
def cvm_bnc_fair_ret2s(panel, features):
    # lean with Binance's last 2s move (MEXC follows within seconds), quotes 38 ticks off Binance's touch
    lean = (features["bnc_ret_2s_cvm"] / 0.647).clip(-20, 20)
    return bl.quote(bid=38, ask=38, size=64, skew=0.2, max_inventory=192, lean=lean,
                    fair=(pl.col("ATUSDT_BINANCE.bid"), pl.col("ATUSDT_BINANCE.ask")))
bnc_ret_2s_cvm
import blinded as bl
from blinded import features as F

x = bl.cross_venue_making(quote="ATUSDT_MEXC", hedge="ATUSDT_BINANCE")


@x.feature("Binance's last 2s mid move (bps): the hedge venue moving through a resting MEXC quote; MEXC follows within seconds")
def bnc_ret_2s_cvm(panel):
    m = F.mid("ATUSDT_BINANCE")
    return (m / F.lag(m, 20) - 1) * 1e4

NOTES.md
# NOTES
Session 1 (speed & information), window=all (in-sample), rankIC @10s:
- lead_gap_5s (Binance 5s ret less MEXC, bps): 0.098 (SE .006), 1s 0.10. Best; hypothesis: MEXC (124bps spread, 1 update/s) catches up to Binance.
- binance_flow_30s (Binance trade_imbalance 30s -> MEXC fwd ret): 0.076 @10s, 0.084 @60s; very persistent (autocorr .997), low turnover.
- mexc_depth_imb (5-level depth imbalance on MEXC): ~0, dead (spread 124bps swamps it).
Caveats: MEXC spread 124bps vs 8bps taker fee -> any taker strategy needs large moves; DATA.md says lead at 100ms is not usable by taker, so use slow horizons (5-60s).
Untried: lead_gap at 1s/30s horizons, Binance depth imbalance (levels 1-4) -> MEXC, Binance microprice minus MEXC mid, theo-minus-MEXC-mid, flow x gap combos.

Session 2 (liquidity & flow), window=all, rankIC:
- theo_gap_mm (theo/MEXC mid -1, bps; cross_venue_making): 1s .044, 10s .099, 60s .069. Best of session; MEXC mid leans toward theo. Use as quote `fair`/skew.
- bnc_micro_mm (Binance microprice-mid, ewm 50 steps; cvm): 10s .059, 60s .049, weak.
- mexc_flow_mm (MEXC 5m trade imbalance; mm): ~0 at 10s (.0002), dead; MEXC flow is one-process noise.
Untried: MEXC queue/touch-size imbalance for mm, spread-width regime (quote only when MEXC spread wide), Binance activity/trade_count as pick-off risk, theo sd_bps/innovation_z.

Session 3 (speed & information), window=all, rankIC:
- basis_gap_z (-(MEXC/Binance log basis bps less its lagged 10min mean); cross_venue_arbitrage): 10s .148, 60s .283 (SE .018). Best so far; slow mean reversion of basis, turnover tiny.
- lead_gap_30s (lead_lag): 10s .118, 60s .127; beats 5s version (.098) at 10s+.
- bnc_depth_imb (order_book_imbalance, F.depth_imbalance("ATUSDT_BINANCE") ewm 50): ZeroDivisionError, error row. Binance depth cols probably need explicit levels/args; check help(F.depth_imbalance) before retrying.
Untried: basis_gap_z with other windows (2min/30min), combine with flow, Binance microprice-based imbalance fixed.

Session 4 (liquidity & flow), window=all, rankIC:
- theo_gap_z_cvm (theo/MEXC gap less lagged 10min mean; cvm): 10s .095, 60s .108 (vs raw theo_gap_mm .099/.069); modest gain at 60s. Not as strong as basis_gap_z (.28 @60s).
- mexc_touch_imb_mm (F.imbalance MEXC, ewm 100): ~0.01-0.015, dead (wide spread swamps queue imbalance).
- bnc_flow_5m_cvm (Binance trade_imbalance 5m): .029 @10s, .038 @60s, weak; 30s version (binance_flow_30s) was better.
Untried: theo gap with 2/30min norm windows, theo sd_bps/innovation_z as quote-width regime (non-directional, feature scoring can't see it), go to strategies using theo_gap_z_cvm as fair/skew.

Session 5 (speed & information), window=all, rankIC:
- basis_gap_z_30m (basis less lagged 30min mean / lagged 30min std, +1): 10s .134, 60s .258 (SE .019); no better than basis_gap_z 10min (.148/.283). Basis norm window not the lever.
- bnc_touch_imb (F.imbalance Binance, ewm 100): submit TIMED OUT (>120s, id 14); ewm_mean over 75k-row-heavy input is slow. Untried; try shorter ewm or roll_mean.
- bnc_flow_60s (trade_imbalance 2m Binance, fill_null 0): dead (~0 at all horizons), unlike 30s (.076). F.signed_volume needs a span arg ("2m"), not a row count (TypeError, id 15).
Untried: basis_gap_z combined with lead_gap_30s (both are catch-up), Binance touch imbalance with cheap smoothing, move to strategies using basis_gap_z (best IC, tiny turnover) -- but 8bps+10bps fees vs ~1.8bps 60s markout is the obstacle.

Session 6 (liquidity & flow), window=all, rankIC (1s/10s/60s):
- theo_gap_per_spread_mm (theo gap / MEXC spread bps; mm): .046/.101/.068 ; ties theo_gap_mm (.099 @10s). Spread scaling adds nothing.

## Streams

## Cross-stream lag

Lag that maximises the correlation of 100 ms log returns over +-500 ms, searched in 10 ms then 1 ms steps. Positive: the first stream moves first. A peak correlation under 0.1 is not a clear peak and its lag is noise.

| first | second | lag_ms | corr_at_lag | corr_at_0 | clear_peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| book ATUSDT_BINANCE | trades ATUSDT_BINANCE | -2 | 0.5334 | 0.5331 | yes |
| book ATUSDT_MEXC | trades ATUSDT_MEXC | 6 | 0.1653 | 0.1653 | yes |
| book ATUSDT_BINANCE | book ATUSDT_MEXC | 23 | 0.3746 | 0.3099 | yes |

## Trade stamps against the book

Share of trades printed at the touch (buy at the ask, sell at the bid) when the book is read just before trade time + offset, offsets -200 to +20 ms in 1 ms steps. A peak at a negative offset means trades are stamped late relative to the book.

| instrument | best_offset_ms | share_at_best | share_at_0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ATUSDT_BINANCE | -1 | 0.796 | 0.6332 |
| ATUSDT_MEXC | 0 | 0.08239 | 0.08239 |

## The touch stream

The fill engine reads every top-of-book row of ATUSDT_MEXC from the touch file `all.touch.parquet` (51,653 rows here), in ticks of 1e-05, and each trade at its own stamp; features never see it. Over this workspace's rows:

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| mid, median; tick | 0.15457; 1e-05 = 0.647 bps |
| spread one tick wide, share of time; two ticks | 0.00%; 0.00% |
| book rows (a second); distinct stamps | 51,653 (1); 51,653 |
| trades (a second) | 3,374 (0.0) |
| displayed at the touch, median bid; ask; bid in USD | 416; 600.8; 64 |
| falls of the best bid; traded out; pulled; partly | 6,126; 0.6%; 99.4%; 0.0% |
| median time between changes of the best bid price | 480.1 ms |
| rows at an unchanged bid price; of them with the bid's size changed | 31,550; 2,842 |

A fall of the best bid is traded out when the sells at the old price from 100 ms before its last row to the fall reach the size it showed, pulled when there were none, and partly each otherwise. Where most levels are traded out, a quote at the back of the touch fills when the level is swept; where many are pulled, the two queue models disagree most.

Every book row of each venue is on the one receive clock; `age_ms` is how long after the exchange's stamp the recorder received it, none where the venue sends no stamp. Over this workspace's rows:

A flow of near-uniform sizes at a regular pace, printing at prices nobody showed as the touch, is one counterparty, not a market: a quote that fills against it fills against that one process, which may change when the quote is there.

## The depth file

`all.depth.parquet` holds ATUSDT_BINANCE's book to 25 levels a side at every snapshot (51,942 rows here), read only by the hedge leg as-of its arrival; its level 0 trails the touch stream by about 100 ms. Over this workspace's rows:

ATUSDT_BINANCE: 75,788 touch rows and 51,942 snapshot rows. The snapshot's level 0 as-of each touch row's stamp plus a lag shows the touch's prices and sizes on 40.5% and 1.2% at 0 ms, 43.3% and 4.6% at 10 ms, 58.8% and 26.6% at 100 ms; the touch as-of each snapshot row shows its level 0 prices on 99.9% and sizes on 99.6% of them (the build refuses under 90%); 18.8% of touch rows cross the as-of snapshot's level 0.

## Venues

ATUSDT_MEXC and ATUSDT_BINANCE are one product on two venues. Venue feed cadence: ATUSDT_BINANCE's book, median gap 1.978 ms between distinct receive stamps; the largest 10 ms bin, 20 to 30 ms, holds 1% of gaps. A lead of the other venue shorter than this cannot be told from the schedule; D11 of the report repeats it on each segment. On the receive clock a lead of one venue over the other can be market lead or feed path.

## Lead-lag on train

C(tau) is the correlation of the leader's last 100 ms log return at each grid point with the follower's 100 ms return ending tau later, over whole steps from -10 to +10 and 10 ms steps across one step either side. A follower that copies with a delay peaks at that delay. `c_after_fill` is C on the follower's first whole step after a taker's fill (50 ms after the decision, so tau = 150 ms), the step a taker holds; `best_after_fill` the largest C from there on; `usable_by_taker` says yes when that is positive and at least half the peak, a rule of thumb.

| leader | follower | lag_at_peak_ms | c_at_peak | c_after_fill | best_after_fill | usable_by_taker |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ATUSDT_MEXC | ATUSDT_BINANCE | -20 | 0.2084 | -0.002106 | 0.002919 | no |
| ATUSDT_BINANCE | ATUSDT_MEXC | 30 | 0.2115 | -0.00278 | 0.01903 | no |

## Pairs on train

Each pair A over B fitted as `bl.pairs` fits it at the brief's defaults: OLS of ln m_A on ln m_B over the trailing 2h, refitted at each 30m clock window. `hedge_ratio` and `residual_sd_bps` are the fit in force at the end of train; `median_half_life_s` is the AR(1) half-life of the spread in each clock window, the median over windows (none when most did not revert), and `no_reversion` the share of windows where it did not come back at all. A pairs feature is scored against the spread return at equal notional, A's forward log return less B's.

| pair | hedge_ratio | residual_sd_bps | median_half_life_s | no_reversion | windows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ATUSDT_MEXC over ATUSDT_BINANCE | 1.141 | 13.3 | 42.31 | 0 | 23 |

## Caveats

- Rows with identical timestamps resolve by file order, last wins.
- Which instruments are in the file, and why, is for the user to own.
- Receive clock: a lead of one stream over another can be market lead or feed delay; these numbers cannot tell them apart.

Built by `blinded demo arb` from the Tardis free day 2026-10-01: ATUSDT spot on `mexc` (instrument ATUSDT_MEXC, the quote venue) and `binance` (ATUSDT_BINANCE, the hedge venue), `book_ticker`, `trades` and `book_snapshot_25` of each, every stamp Tardis's `local_timestamp`, the recorder's receive clock. The data file keeps every book row of both venues, with `age_ms`, how long after the exchange's stamp the recorder received the row (0 where the venue sends none), the hedge venue's levels 1 to 4 from its snapshot as-of each of its rows, and every trade with its own venue's touch as received. Nothing is thinned: the quote venue changes its touch about once a second, and the hedge leg reads the hedge venue's touch at fill stamps that are on no lattice. The touch file `tardis-arb-atusdt-mexc-binance-2026-10-01.touch.parquet` holds every two-sided row of ATUSDT_MEXC in ticks of 1e-05; the depth file `tardis-arb-atusdt-mexc-binance-2026-10-01.depth.parquet` every snapshot row of ATUSDT_BINANCE, 25 levels a side in price units. Only the sims read the two. Ticks: ATUSDT_MEXC 1e-05, ATUSDT_BINANCE 0.0001; lot 1.0 on the quote venue. Fees in the brief: maker 0 and taker 8 bps on the quote venue (its exchangeInfo), the hedge 10 bps (Binance's regular spot tier); the stock block's `withdrawal_fee_coin` is unset: look it up on both venues' withdrawal pages before an arbitrage strategy is scored.

The quote venue's spread on the other free days in the raw directory, time-weighted median: 2026-09-01: 112.0 bps; 2026-08-01: 11.3 bps; 2026-07-01: 8.0 bps. A wide day is a month with no maker on the quote venue; the build refuses a day under three hedge fees.

## The theo

`F.theo("ATUSDT")` is a Kalman filter's consolidated price of ATUSDT over ATUSDT_MEXC, ATUSDT_BINANCE: one latent log price and one basis per venue, each quote a reading of the two with its own noise; the anchor (ATUSDT_BINANCE 1) fixes the origin, so the theo is quoted in the anchor's terms. It was computed once at init, causally, one event at a time, and is a column of the panel (`THEO.ATUSDT.theo`, `.sd_bps`, `.innovation_z`, `.basis_<venue>`).

Fitted on train only, by the prediction-error likelihood on its stream conflated to one event per venue per second (10,178 events, 201 evaluations, negative log likelihood -67,642.2): price volatility 1.72 bps per sqrt-second, quote noise ATUSDT_MEXC 1.4, ATUSDT_BINANCE 7.71 bps, event-clock weight 0.316; the basis wander held at 0.02 bps per sqrt-second, not fitted.

| segment | venue | events | z mean | z variance | z lag-1 autocorrelation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| train | ATUSDT_MEXC | 11,553 | -0.039 | 1.234 | 0.354 |
| train | ATUSDT_BINANCE | 11,281 | +0.066 | 0.773 | 0.920 |
| val | ATUSDT_MEXC | 18,390 | +0.043 | 3.494 | 0.321 |
| val | ATUSDT_BINANCE | 38,612 | -0.029 | 1.350 | 0.952 |
| test | ATUSDT_MEXC | 21,176 | +0.008 | 4.528 | 0.273 |
| test | ATUSDT_BINANCE | 25,065 | -0.079 | 2.176 | 0.958 |

A filter that fits gives z of mean 0, variance 1 and no autocorrelation; validation and test are filtered with train's parameters, so a regime change shows there as innovations that stop being white.
